insight.title: How a distant cloud reshaped the human path
insight.subtitle: A quiet story about the invisible threads that tie nature to our inventions.

sections.text: In 1815, a distant volcano threw a veil of ash across the sky, dimming the sun for an entire year. Across the globe, crops failed and stables went empty. In that cold silence, the world shifted. We needed a new way to move without the help of hungry horses.

To solve the crisis, a German inventor built a wooden frame with two wheels. He called it a running machine. It did not require oats or hay, only the rhythm of human legs. This simple balance transformed our anatomy into an engine. By removing the horse, we finally discovered our own momentum.

This moment reminds us that the world is a single, delicate web. A tremor in the mountains can spark a revolution in the city. We often think we lead the way with our bright ideas. Yet, more often, we are simply learning how to dance with the unexpected turns of nature.

news.title: AI-assisted decision support system improves stroke care and long-term outcomes
news.description: A clinical decision support tool that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze scans after a stroke alongside treatment recommendations is associated with better quality care and long term outcomes for patients compared with usual care, finds a study from China published by The BMJ today.

news.title: Replacing sedentary time improves insulin resistance in adolescents
news.description: Adolescents who replaced just half an hour of sedentary behaviors, such as sitting on the couch or spending time at the computer, each day for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity or sleep may lower their insulin resistance, a key factor in preventing the development of Type 2 diabetes, according to preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's EPI|Lifestyle Scientific Sessions 2026.

news.title: Digital decision support tool improves outcomes in colorectal surgery
news.description: Research published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology provides robust evidence for the use of a digital visualization and decision support tool in colorectal (bowel) surgery.

news.title: Don’t Drink Apple Juice: Why Whole Apples Are Healthier
news.description: Experts warn that apple juice lacks fibre and is high in sugar, causing blood sugar spikes and reduced satiety. Eating whole apples with peel offers better benefits, including improved heart, gut, and liver health, and lower colon cancer risk. Studies link whole fruit intake to better outcomes, while excess fruit juice may increase long-term health risks. , Health, Times Now
